['Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

However, you still have the right to necesarry medical care, judicial assistance and children under 18 have to right to attend school as well.  

You can choose to apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.  

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', "Document: Amsterdam (e-mail !)

HSP is closed Ukrainians in Amsterdam can report to the municipality directly via opvangoekraine@amsterdam.nl   

Sometimes, the person may initially receive a rejection due to the current situation in NL.

We recommend following up on the response and continuing communication with the municipality via the same email.

In your follow-up, kindly explain your situation, where you're staying, and how long you can stay there.

Also, include any important details about your circumstances, such as medical conditions, young children, or other special needs", "Document: GGD Center for Sexual Health in Amsterdam You can talk to the GGD about every topic concerning your body, your relations and sex.

They can provide care regarding your sexual health, sexual orientation, gender issues,  sexwork or sexual violence.

Come in to talk about ways to protect yourself with  PEP/PrEP, contraception and vaccinations.

This is a LHBT-friendly centre.

You don't need  ID / BSN / health-insurance.  

You have to call or use the website link to make an appointment.   

Everyone is welcome, the care is free of charge.

You do not need a referral by a doctor.   

All healthcare workers have professional secrecy.  

https://afspraak.ggdaphrodite.nl/?lang=en   Phone: (020) 555 5822  Address: GGD Amsterdam Centrum voor Seksuele Gezondheid Nieuwe Achtergracht 100 1018 WT Amsterdam (near Weesperplein metro station)", 'Document: I am a transperson, where can I get support?

If you need trans care, you can contact the Trans United trans clinic, a community initiative with support from the GGD Amsterdam:  https://transunitedeurope.eu/?page_id=255  

For more information see:  - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100298-living-in-the-netherlands-as-an-lgbtqia-individual - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100299-activities-for-the-lgbtqia-community', 'Document: I need medical treatment in the Netherlands and an I am abroad  Many people in Ukraine lack access to the medical care they need.

This can be for all kinds of diseases, like cancer treatment, but also for wounds caused by grenades, bullets or mines.   

For a detailed step-by-step guide on handling cases where PAs abroad want to come to the Netherlands, see below.  

## Important notes  - There are two main categories of people wanting to come to NL for medical treatment.

Always ask the PA about their goal of coming to the Netherlands:  1.

Coming to the Netherlands for temporary treatment and then returning to Ukraine: Since the start of the war, the EU has designed a standard procedure for Ukrainians in need of urgent medical care.

The patients must be applied by their doctor for one of the following programs: Medevac Coordination Center (Civil) or Medical Forces Command (Military).

EU countries (NL included) will receive these applications and can decide to accept the case, after which the patient will be brought to a medical hub in Poland and then transferred to the country that accepted.', "Document: I need medical treatment and I am in the Netherlands.

What can I do?  

All hospitals in the Netherlands provide medical care for Ukrainian refugees, including Ukrainian PAs with cancer.

They can continue their treatment in the Netherlands, in consultation with a doctor.  

First, you need to visit a general practitioner (GP), who will refer you to the hospital if necessary.

If you have your medical file, bring it with you as it can be helpful.

Having a Dutch-speaking person assist you can also make the process easier, but it is not mandatory.   

For more information on finding a GP, see the questions under the sub-category 'doctor' or click [here](https://agreeable-forest-090d2f903.4.azurestaticapps.net/ukraine/health-wellbeing/doctor)  

For most recent information on cancer treatment see: https://www.kanker.nl/nieuwsberichten/gratis-kankerzorg-voor-oekraiense-vluchtelingen", 'Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Every person in need, regardless of background and papers, is welcome at the Humanitarian Service Point in the Amsterdam office of The Netherlands Red Cross.

For everyone who visits, the situation is examined and a possible solution is sought.

To find a solution, the Red Cross is also dependent on available assistance from other organizations.', 'Document: Will I still receive care if I do not apply for asylum?

If you do not want to go through the asylum procedure or your asylum application has been rejected, you will be responsible for the costs of care yourself from 4 March 2024.

If you are unable to pay the costs of medically necessary care, the healthcare provider can appeal to the Subsidy Scheme for Medically Necessary Care for Uninsured Persons (SOV) or the Uninsurable Scheme (OVV) (https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/).', 'Document: Do I still receive healthcare?

You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.

How that care is paid for depends on the situation.', 'Document: Do I need health insurance?

For displaced persons from Ukraine, basic healthcare and urgent medical care are covered.

As of 1 July 2022, displaced persons from Ukraine with a BSN will be covered by the Medical Care for Displaced Persons Regulation (RMO).

For more information about RMO see: https://www.rmoekraine.nl/Zorgverleners/over-RMO  You do need to take out health insurance when you start working in the Netherlands.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100084-you-are-entitled-to-healthcare-through-the-rmo  https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/actueel/nieuws/2022/06/29/zorgverzekering-ontheemden-oekraine-verandert', 'Document: All information shared is kept confidential.

The support offered by FairWork is free of charge.

See: www.fairwork.nu.   

Potential victims are entitled to the assistance of a lawyer.

Specialised counsellors can make referrals.

If a (migration) lawyer is already in place, it is advisable to discuss possible trafficking/exploitation with him/her.   

After a crime such as human trafficking, but also in cases of (sexual) violence, for example, it is possible to report it.

Undocumented migrants also have the right to report safely to the specialised police department (AVIM).

For undocumented migrants, we recommend going to the police together with a social worker.

Specialised social workers can provide information on the reporting procedure    In cases of human trafficking in the Netherlands (sometimes also within EU), victims who report human trafficking are entitled to assistance and protection, such as shelter and a temporary residence permit.

There are conditions attached to this.

For more information see: [Ondersteunen van slachtoffers |Wegwijzer mensenhandel](https://www.wegwijzermensenhandel.nl/ondersteunen-van-slachtoffers)', "Document: Huisartsenpost Amsterdam When you are in Amsterdam you can call or visit this place if you feel very sick outside of times that regular health services are open.  

+31 88 - 00 30 600 (17:00 - 08:00)  https://www.huisartsenpostenamsterdam.nl/  

If it's life-threatening: Call 112 instead!", 'Document: I need an orthodontist, where can I go and is it reimbursed?  

In principle, the orthodontist will not be reimbursed.

The 16 orthodontic practices of TopOrtho in the Netherlands offer orthodontic emergency care up to €250 free of charge to refugees.     

For most recent information and to maken an appointment see: https://www.toportho.nl/emergency-dental-care-for-ukrainian-refugees-in-the-netherlands/', "Document: Where can I find general information about healthcare in The Netherlands?

For an overview of questions about your own healthcare or your family's, you can go to the website of the Dutch government: https://www.government.nl/topics/themes/family-health-and-care   For an infografic about primary care in the Netherlands see: [NL](https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/infographic-eerstelijnszorg-nederlands-versie-voor-oekraiense-ontheemden/)

[UA](https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/infographic-eerstelijnszorg-oekraiens/)  For an overview of educational materials in different languages [click here](https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf)  

For an information video about healthcare in the Netherlands by the Red Cross choose your language below: [EN](https://youtu.be/cQogocKtJ-o)

[UA](https://youtu.be/3Bf7Riv8YuY)", 'Document: Where can I find healthcare for my child?  

The JGZ (youth healthcare) is responsible for preventive care for children, including those of refugees.

The JGZ provides physical, cognitive and psychosocial screenings and provides vaccinations in accordance with the National Vaccination Programme.   

Displaced persons from the Ukraine in the Netherlands can make use of this care free of charge.

Please contact the youth healthcare department of the regional GGD or JGZ organisation.  

An overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg', 'Document: In the evening / office hours; check urgency and if it can wait for the next day.

['Document: Crisis shelter "Stay away from my Body" (Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis) Did you flee because of domestic or relational violence?

The crisis shelter of "Stay away from my body" can help you.

Call for free: 0800 0117.', 'Document: Can the Red Cross provide me with a place to live?

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

This is done by the municipality.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

You should go to one of the registration points to get shelter.   

For more information, please see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/109-shelter', 'Document: What facilities should be available at a Crisis Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -

Access to medical care - Third party insurance  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Space for children  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.', 'Document: What facilities should be available at an Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -', 'Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?  

Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

You can always share these links with the PA as well.

See also below what the general explanation is.   

General advice  If you want to apply for Temporary Protection and need help with a shelter place, visit a municipality ("gemeente" in Dutch).

Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

(Please check the latest Temporary Protection rules on [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-chtoby-poluchit-vremennuyu-zashchitu-vy-dolzhny-sootvetstvovat-etim-usloviyam).)', 'Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.', "Document: You are still allowed to open your home to displaced persons.

In the Government's Guidelines, you will find important information: https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/publicaties/2022/04/15/handreiking-particuliere-opvang-oekrainers-poo  Thank you again for your offer and for opening your home.

We hope you can help someone in need.  

Kind regards, Red Cross Shelter Team", 'Document: What happens at the end of the stay with a host family?  

If the stay at a private shelter ends, you can choose from three options (see sub-questions).', 'Document: Can I change a shelter (because conditions are not nice, or to be closer to work, or to be closer to family and friends, or because I want to live in the city/in the countryside/in a different place, etc.)?

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.', 'Document: Another host shelter You can look for a new host family.

You can do this through your social network or through various local initiatives.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.', 'Document: I had already applied to be considered for placement.

What happens now?

Unfortunately, due to the termination of the project, RefugeeHomeNL is no longer able to offer you a placement.

You still retain the right to receive support in the Netherlands.  - If you are currently staying in a Municipal Shelter and seeking an alternative, please inquire with the municipality where you are residing for available options.

- If you are currently in private shelter and looking for alternatives, please consult the municipality where you are staying for further guidance.

- Apart from Municipal and Private Accommodation, you can also explore finding independent housing, such as rentals, purchases, boarding houses, hostels, etc. -

If you are currently in Ukraine or another country and planning to come to the Netherlands, you can find information here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/126-arrival-in-the-netherlands   Need help for shelter of housing in the Netherlands?

Visit http://www.refugeehelp.nl for comprehensive information on available options for shelter and housing in the Netherlands.

VluchtelingenWerk Nederland provides various means of contact for additional help and advice.', 'Document: What does a Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) offer?

Humanitarian Service Points are run by the Red Cross.

At a Humanitarian Service Point you can rest, eat and drink something, and charge your phone.

You will receive further information about how shelter is arranged in the Netherlands, and the journey onward.

Humanitarian Service Points are not registration locations.

They are intended as a place where you can rest and to help you on your way.

At a registration location, the municipality determines who does and does not have access to shelter and you are registered.

At Humanitarian Service Points, Red Cross employees inform you about the options for shelter, but they do not determine any policies.', "Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).", 'Document: Can I stay in the shelter with my pet?  

Yes, you can.

However, please note that centers are overcrowded, and space for pets is very limited.

Availability depends on the municipality.

Therefore it is very possible that there is no place for you and the pet together.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100049-pets', 'Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

However, you will have to pay a contribution.

You can also move to other accommodation, for instance with a host family, friends or family members, or at a hotel.  

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income', "Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You receive the money in their bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.', 'Document: I had already applied to be considered for placement.

What happens now?

Unfortunately, due to the termination of the project, RefugeeHomeNL is no longer able to offer you a placement.

You still retain the right to receive support in the Netherlands.  - If you are currently staying in a Municipal Shelter and seeking an alternative, please inquire with the municipality where you are residing for available options.

- If you are currently in private shelter and looking for alternatives, please consult the municipality where you are staying for further guidance.

Visit http://www.refugeehelp.nl for comprehensive information on available options for shelter and housing in the Netherlands.

VluchtelingenWerk Nederland provides various means of contact for additional help and advice.', 'Document: What does a Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) offer?

Yes, you can.

However, please note that centers are overcrowded, and space for pets is very limited.

Availability depends on the municipality.

Therefore it is very possible that there is no place for you and the pet together.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100049-pets', 'Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

However, you will have to pay a contribution.

You can also move to other accommodation, for instance with a host family, friends or family members, or at a hotel.  

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income', "Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You receive the money in their bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods.  

Living allowance may be payed out in kind by local authorities (for example when meals are offered).

For most recent information see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income", 'Document: Access to medical care - Third party insurance - Living allowance (if asylum procedure has started) - Public transportation card - Education and development program - Payment of extraordinary expenses  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Locker - Night light - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Small towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Baby lotion - Washing up liquid - Washing machine detergent - Space for children - Space for men - Space for women  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: What is the difference between crisis emergency shelters and emergency shelters?

Below you will find more information on what facilities should be present at the different types of reception.   

Please note: this overview is based on information from COA, COA arranges reception for refugees not covered by the Temporary Protection Directive.

input: I just arrived from Ukraine and the HUB is closed. Where can I go to register for shelter now? I don't know what to do.
context:
['Document: Rotterdam (CLOSED!)  

Please note!

Due to overcrowding and insufficient capacity, the HUB in Rotterdam is closed for an indefinite period.

As an exception, this HUB will continue to assist Ukrainians with a connection to Rotterdam or the surrounding region.

For example, because your children already go to school here.  

address: Marten Meesweg 141B,  Rotterdam.  

e-mail opvang@rotterdam.nl.   

Openning times: - Monday to Tuesday: 10:00 -15:00  - Wednesday to Friday: 10:00 - 14:00  - Saturday & Sunday : closed   [Rotterdam website](https://www.rotterdam.nl/vluchtelingen-oekraine)  

Extra advice – "Vraagwijzer": You can visit the Vraagwijzer for free help and advice about administration, parenting, laws, money, or health.

There are several locations in the city, including the [Ukrainian House](https://www.wmoradar.nl/district/oekraiens-huis/) at Pleinweg 196A.', 'Document: Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine', 'Document: Can I switch to Mrija, the temporary neighbourhood in Vlaardingen municipality?

Mrija houses Ukrainian people accommodated in Vlaardingen and the other municipalities in the Rotterdam-Rijnmond region in (emergency) shelters or with host families.

However, Ukrainian people cannot apply for housing in Mrija themselves.

The houses will be distributed via the regional coordination point for displaced persons from Ukraine, in consultation with the municipality of Vlaardingen, which will give the final permission.  

If you would like to be considered for a home, please contact the location management of your current shelter location.

Do you live in a host family?

Then please approach the contact person in your municipality.', 'Document: Netherlands (but not Amsterdam/Utrecht/Swolgen/Heerevenveen/Rotterdam/Haarlem) General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

To apply, visit the municipality office in the city where you will arrive.  

Please note that the housing situation here is challenging and becoming more restricted.

We recommend contacting us before you leave to get the latest updates.  

If possible, try to arrange accommodation on your own when arriving in the Netherlands.

Note that you need a local address (accommodation) to apply for temporary protection.   

Actions to take when general advise was not sufficient NO referrals for cases outside of the Netherlands.

Advise the PA to contact us upon arrival.   

Actions to take when general advise is not sufficient If the PA shares challenges in finding a place to stay, please consult with the Team Captain.', 'Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?  

Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.', "Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

Are you or your family member passing through the Netherlands or visiting relatives?

Then you cannot make use of the municipal shelter for Ukrainian displaced persons and you are not entitled to an allowance.

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

Explanation of situation: Since the end of February 2024, the shelters for displaced people from Ukraine are (almost) full.

Most of the registration locations are closed, which makes it confusing for people arriving to the Netherlands where to go.

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Below, you can find the most important steps to take in order to help someone on their way.   

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

- Check where this person has already been, did they just arrive?  

- Are they already registered in a municipality (BRP)?  

- Did they try another option to find shelter before going to NLRC office?   

Step 2: contact CHV shelter / someone from the shelter program: - If you are in an office in the district: contact the CHV specifically for shelter.

You can find a list of the CHV'ers", 'Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.   

Actions to take when general advice is not sufficient If the general advice isn’t enough, forward the case to the team captain.  

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.', 'Document: What do I say when someone offers to host a displaced person from Ukraine?

Dear [Name],  Thank you to those who have offered their support.

(adjust to the question)

This means that we are currently unable to match host households with Ukrainian displaced persons.  

If you would like to open your home to Ukrainian displaced persons, we recommend that you inform your local municipality.

Sometimes, you can assist the municipality in this way, or they may know of a local initiative that is looking for host households for Ukrainian displaced persons.

Displaced persons often also reach out to local church communities, where you can also offer your help.  

You are still allowed to open your home to displaced persons.', 'Document: Abroad  General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

To apply, visit the municipality office in the city where you will arrive.  

Please note that the housing situation here is challenging and becoming more restricted.

We recommend contacting us before you leave to get the latest updates.  

If possible, try to arrange accommodation on your own when arriving in the Netherlands.

Note that you need a local address (accommodation) to apply for temporary protection.   

Actions to take when general advise was not sufficient NO referrals for cases outside of the Netherlands.

Advise the PA to contact us upon arrival.', "Document: What can I do if I don't feel comfortable at my host family?

I am sorry to hear this.

Sharing a household can be challenging, especially if there are cultural differences in lifestyle, food, manners or rules.    

If you do not feel safe at your host family, you can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities.

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.   

For additonal information about safety, see https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100105-safety-in-the-netherlands", 'Document: Refugeehelp The Dutch Council for Refugees has created an online platform called RefugeeHelp.  

It contains a lot of general information for all Ukrainian refugees who have arrived in the Netherlands.  

The information is available in English, Ukrainian, Russian and Dutch.  

https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee', 'Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

This applies to both refugees who have been in the Netherlands for some time and new arrivals.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.   

[*Dutch Government website*](https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay)', 'Document: Ukrainian Women Refugee Association Ukrainian Women Refugee Association in the Netherlands in het Oekraïens en Engels:   https://unitedway.nl/uwra/', 'Document: For the most recent information, see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine or https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100082-leaving-the-netherlands-temporarily', 'Document: For more information, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100041-return-to-ukraine', 'Document: For more information in Ukrainian, see: https://open.overheid.nl/repository/ronl-4907d802ea0f813cf0ca978d64d3e64735a071ed/1/pdf/Kinderopvang%20voor%20vluchtelingen%20uit%20Oekra_ne%20_Ukrainian_.pdf', 'Document: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100008-studying', 'Document: Can my child go to a Ukrainian school in the Netherlands?  

Yes, that is possible.

Currently, there are 10 Ukrainian weekend schools in The Netherlands:  - Almere - Amsterdam - Eindhoven - Groningen - Haarlem - Oegstgeest - Rotterdam - Utrecht - Zoetermeer  

For more information, see: https://ukrainians.nl/pages/community.html#anchor-schools']

Actions to take when general advise is not sufficient If the PA shares challenges in finding a place to stay, please consult with the Team Captain.', "Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

In general, houses are expensive, because there is a large housing shortage in the Netherlands, especially in the larger cities.   

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.  

Places where private homes are offered: Funda, AirBNB, Marktplaats website, Facebook groups per city (search for 'I'm looking for a home').   

For most recent information see: [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing)  and [renting a house](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house)", "Document: Utrecht (e-mail !)

yes or no

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.', 'Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

['Document: Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine', 'Document: Who is responsible for the shelter of children travelling alone from Ukraine?

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

They always have to get shelter right away.

The municipality has to call with Nidos.

Nidos then conducts an intake with the minor—and, where possible, remotely with the parents—to determine whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine', 'Document: Can the Red Cross provide me with a place to live?

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

This is done by the municipality.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

You should go to one of the registration points to get shelter.   

For more information, please see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/109-shelter', 'Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.', 'Document: What is the difference between crisis emergency shelters and emergency shelters?

Below you will find more information on what facilities should be present at the different types of reception.   

Please note: this overview is based on information from COA, COA arranges reception for refugees not covered by the Temporary Protection Directive.

Therefore, the facilities for displaced persons from Ukraine may differ in practice.', 'Document: General Info and Basic Instructions for TP & shelter Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

You can always share these links with the PA as well.

See also below what the general explanation is.   

General Information  TP is valid until March 2027.

In principle, this means that displaced people from Ukraine should be helped during this time.

However, the housing situation is difficult, especially within municipal shelters.

Therefore:  1.

If PA does not need help with shelter, and can afford a place to stay (even for a few days): PA can look for a place themselves.

PA has to check if they can register at the accommodation and also at the municipality.  

2.

If PA needs help with finding shelter, please know that the situation is currently very difficult and becoming more restricted.   

3.', 'Document: What facilities should be available at a Crisis Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -

Access to medical care - Third party insurance  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Space for children  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: Can I change a shelter (because conditions are not nice, or to be closer to work, or to be closer to family and friends, or because I want to live in the city/in the countryside/in a different place, etc.)?

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.', 'Document: Access to medical care - Third party insurance - Living allowance (if asylum procedure has started) - Public transportation card - Education and development program - Payment of extraordinary expenses  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Locker - Night light - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Small towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Baby lotion - Washing up liquid - Washing machine detergent - Space for children - Space for men - Space for women  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: What facilities should be available at an Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -', "Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

Are you or your family member passing through the Netherlands or visiting relatives?

Then you cannot make use of the municipal shelter for Ukrainian displaced persons and you are not entitled to an allowance.

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

A host family is not obliged to accommodate family visits.", 'Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?  

Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

You can always share these links with the PA as well.

See also below what the general explanation is.   

General advice  If you want to apply for Temporary Protection and need help with a shelter place, visit a municipality ("gemeente" in Dutch).

Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

(Please check the latest Temporary Protection rules on [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-chtoby-poluchit-vremennuyu-zashchitu-vy-dolzhny-sootvetstvovat-etim-usloviyam).)', 'Document: What happens at the end of the stay with a host family?  

If the stay at a private shelter ends, you can choose from three options (see sub-questions).', "Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).", 'Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

However, you will have to pay a contribution.

You can also move to other accommodation, for instance with a host family, friends or family members, or at a hotel.

['Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.', "Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?  

The Non-residents Records Database (RNI) is a part of the Personal Records Database (BRP).

It is a register of people who do not live in the Netherlands, no longer live in the Netherlands or live in the Netherlands for less than 4 months.

For example migrant / seasonal workers register in the RNI.   

If you are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).  

For most recent information see:  https://www.nederlandwereldwijd.nl/rni/wat-is-rni  https://www.rvig.nl/basisregistratie-personen https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/richtlijn-tijdelijke-bescherming-oekraine#bewijs-van-verblijf-", "Document: Can I get proof of residence if I have a BSN number that I got with a RNI registration?

- Check where somebody lives, and always try to find a GP most close by – so in a bigger city, also check this on neighborhood level.  - It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend.  

-

In the evening / office hours; check urgency and if it can wait for the next day.', "Document: Where can I go when I have special care needs?

To receive specialist care, you often first need a referral from your General Practitioner (GP).

So you can often not just go to the hospital itself for your medical problems.

Do you need specialist care?

Then make sure that you first visit a GP so that you can be referred.

See the questions under 'Doctor' for more information on how to find a GP.   

In the subquestions you can find an overview of organisations that help people with special needs and disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100098-care-for-people-with-disabilities", 'Document: I have temporary protection in one EU country but want to move to another for a job.

The new country refuses to register me since I’m already registered elsewhere.

What can I do?          

You are free to choose the EU country in which you enjoy temporary protection.

However, you can benefit from temporary protection only in one EU Member State at a time.

The rights connected to temporary protection are the same in every EU country bound by the Directive.  

If you have registered in one country and decide to move to another, you need to inform the authorities of the country in which you are currently registered.

The country where you move will then register you and offer you the temporary protection status and subsequent rights.   

Please note that if you had a temporary work visa for the Netherlands and are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.', "Document: How do I find a General Practitioner during working hours?

For people who are staying at a host (family):   First check whether you can go to the host's General Practitioner (GP).

Sometimes GPs no longer accept patients, so you have to look for another GP.

Do you not know how to find a general practitioner?

Then you can ask the municipality that you are staying in where the closest general practitioner is that can help you.    

For people who are in an emergency shelter:    We advise you to contact the medical facilities that are present there.

For example, Doctors of the World visits various emergency shelters.

The shelters themselves are better aware of this.   

You can get medical help if you are uninsured.

This is reimbursed by means of a special subsidy.

Sometimes GPs don't know this.

You can refer them to [the website of the CAK](https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag).

However, this website is difficult to understand, so explain that they can show this website to the GP

but they don't need to understand it themselves.", "Document: Where can I find a General Practitioner during the evening, night and weekends?

In the evening, at night or at the weekend you can contact the GP at the 'huisartesenpost' for urgent questions.   

For the addresses and phone numbers, see: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisartsenpost", "Document: I need medical treatment and I am in the Netherlands.

What can I do?  

All hospitals in the Netherlands provide medical care for Ukrainian refugees, including Ukrainian PAs with cancer.

They can continue their treatment in the Netherlands, in consultation with a doctor.  

First, you need to visit a general practitioner (GP), who will refer you to the hospital if necessary.

If you have your medical file, bring it with you as it can be helpful.

Having a Dutch-speaking person assist you can also make the process easier, but it is not mandatory.   

For more information on finding a GP, see the questions under the sub-category 'doctor' or click [here](https://agreeable-forest-090d2f903.4.azurestaticapps.net/ukraine/health-wellbeing/doctor)  

For most recent information on cancer treatment see: https://www.kanker.nl/nieuwsberichten/gratis-kankerzorg-voor-oekraiense-vluchtelingen", 'Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine', 'Document: Can I register my newborn baby for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

Yes you can.

Within three days after the birth of a child, you have to report this to the municipality.

After registration you will receive a birth certificate.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth', 'Document: In the evening / office hours; check urgency and if it can wait for the next day.

Explain that somebody can always call 112 or go to the huisartsenpost.   

- Check really well if information is clear and if they can follow up with the information that you provided.

Let them know they can always come back when they face issues or do not receive the right help.   

Do you have an emergency?

Call 112 or go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital.  

In the next two questions you can find information on how to find a GP.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100072-this-is-how-the-dutch-healthcare-system-works', 'Document: I have tuberculosis, what should I do?  

Contact your General Practitioner (GP) or contact the tuberculosis control department of the Municipal Public Health Services (GGD) directly.

Specialist doctors and nurses will screen you for tuberculosis.

If you have tuberculosis, you will be prescribed medication.

The nurses at the GGD will help you take the medication correctly.  

For more information see: https://www.rivm.nl/node/200571', "Document: GGD Center for Sexual Health in Amsterdam You can talk to the GGD about every topic concerning your body, your relations and sex.

They can provide care regarding your sexual health, sexual orientation, gender issues,  sexwork or sexual violence.

Come in to talk about ways to protect yourself with  PEP/PrEP, contraception and vaccinations.

This is a LHBT-friendly centre.

You don't need  ID / BSN / health-insurance.  

You have to call or use the website link to make an appointment.   

Everyone is welcome, the care is free of charge.

You do not need a referral by a doctor.   

All healthcare workers have professional secrecy.  

https://afspraak.ggdaphrodite.nl/?lang=en   Phone: (020) 555 5822  Address: GGD Amsterdam Centrum voor Seksuele Gezondheid Nieuwe Achtergracht 100 1018 WT Amsterdam (near Weesperplein metro station)", 'Document: Another host shelter You can look for a new host family.

You can do this through your social network or through various local initiatives.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.', "Document: The doctor will determine whether this is necessary.  

3)

If the doctor does not want to arrange a translator or don't know how to do this, you can show the website mentioned before (https://www.zoschakeltueentolkin.nl/)   

For more information, check the links below: - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100075-this-is-how-healthcare-works - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100398-what-you-need-to-know-if-you-have-a-healthcare-appointment-and-do-not-speak-dutch"]

['Document: Food support per city The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of food options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', "Document: How can I get food support?  

When you are staying in a public shelter, please approach someone from the shelter to ask where you can find additional food support.

You can also contact the Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk.

For all general questions, new applications, extension requests, etc, PA's can call/text/

WhatsApp them at +31 97010259797 (Mon-Fri 9:00 – 17:00).  

In municipalities all over the country Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands) distributes food parcels to displaced persons from Ukraine.

Too find out if you are eligible, please see: https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/", "Document: I can't eat the same food as my host does

Yes, I understand that you used to eat different meals and some food can taste strange for you.

If so, you can always discuss it with your host.

I am sure, there is a way for both of you to find a balance.

For example, you can ask your host if it's not a problem for you to cook some meals for yourself.

If you already get social money, you can buy some products for your own use.

It's not an obligation to eat only the food your host eats every day.

You can use your money for food you prefer to eat.", 'Document: Red Cross The Red Cross focuses on humanitarian assistance, they offer for example; first aid, emergency food support and psychosocial support.  

Through the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp (https://wa.me/31614458781]) they can connect you to available help.', 'Document: Google Map with an overview of locations where humanitarian aid is being provided (e.g. food, clothing) https://goo.gl/maps/SvfGnjBnH8j9cYbA9', 'Document: Helpdesk Red Cross If you have questions regarding food, shelter, medical help, your situation or any other help you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp

[here](https://wa.me/31614458781)  General helpdesk from the Red Cross, we can help to connect you with the right help available.', 'Document: How can I get support with clothes?  

The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  

https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/  For most recent information on initiatives that provide support in clothes or offer clothes for a small price see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace', 'Document: I have HIV, where can I get support?

You can contact Service point of the Hiv Association and a volunteer from the association can answer your questions.   

https://www.hivvereniging.nl/blog/belangenbeschijning/13701-hoe-zit-het-met-hiv-zorg-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Phone: 020 - 689 25 77 (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 22:00)   

Email: servicepunt@hivvereniging.nl', 'Document: I have an eye condition, where can I get support?

The Eye Association advises and refers to the right authorities.

It can be about:  - Access to eye care: think of eye drops, injections or other treatments - Living with a visual impairment in the Netherlands: think of tools or building a network and learning the language  https://www.oogvereniging.nl/standpunten/steunpunt-migranten/steunpunt-oekraiense-vluchtelingen/

Telephone: 030-2945444  Email: ooglijn@oogvereniging.nl', 'Document: Website about financial support for Ukrainians during the war https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua/article/grosova-dopomoga-ukraincam-pid-cas-vijni-7738', 'Document: EnableMe UA EnableMe UA is a complete, up-to-date guide on all issues of disability and a friendly community for Ukrainians with special needs, mental disorders, chronic diseases and various disability groups.   

EnableMe Ukraine offers information, advice and online support to people with physical, mental or psychological disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua', 'Document: Is dental care reimbursed?  

This depends on your situation.  

Below is an overview of dental services that are covered by the insurance for Ukrainian displaced persons (RMO):   Conditions for providing dental care to Ukrainian displaced persons:  i.

The clinic can help patients living (registered) within a radius of 50 km from the clinic.  ii.

The patient must make an appointment through the special organization Tandartslijn (tel. 0881122112).  

iii.

If necessary, the clinic must provide proof of the record and argue the urgency (urgent necessity) of providing assistance.  

iv.

These conditions apply to adults and children.  

v. Compensation for adults

is limited to an amount of 250 euros per year and the choice of treatment - elimination of emergency pain with minimal costs.  

vi.

The amount of treatment is not limited to children under 18 years of age.

The only limitation is the exclusion of orthodontic treatment and prosthetics with implants and porcelain-ceramic crowns.   

The following types of dental services are covered by the RMO scheme:  i. Non-Periodic Review Consultation  ii.', 'Document: What is the stance of the Red Cross when somebody is not helped at HSP?  

We do our best to ensure that people arriving at an Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) are directed to the most appropriate form of assistance for them.

This could mean that people are directed to Ter Apel, rather than assistance being provided at the HSP.

However, we try to ensure that all refugees have their basic needs met, i.e. they can have some food and a drink, rest and charge mobile devices before travelling onwards.', 'Document: Access to medical care - Third party insurance - Living allowance (if asylum procedure has started) - Public transportation card - Education and development program - Payment of extraordinary expenses  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Locker - Night light - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Small towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Baby lotion - Washing up liquid - Washing machine detergent - Space for children - Space for men - Space for women  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: I want to return to Ukraine, where can I find support?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine who wish to return or continue their migration can receive assistance from the Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V).

Depending on the nationality and/or country of return or onward migration, they can provide return and/or reintegration support.                   

For more information in English and Ukranian, see: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine   You can use the contact form on the bottom of the following webpage of the DT&V to indicate whether you would like to be assisted in your return to Ukraine: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine   For an information video made by the Red Cross see: EN: https://youtu.be/PV-PJv-oCDw  UA: https://youtu.be/5YsAYFqYsjM  RUS: https://youtu.be/n_otbQncTHs', 'Document: Can I get financial support for a return to my country of origin?

If you have fled Ukraine, but do not have Ukrainian citizenship, you can no longer make use of the remigration support of the Repatriation & Departure Service (DT&V).

This financial support stopped March 4, 2024.   

Are you a third-country national from Ukraine and do you still want to return to your country of origin or another country outside the European Union?

IOM can assist you with REAN-return support and depending on your nationality you might be eligible for additional reintegration assistance offered by IOM and several non-gouvernemental organisations.  

The IOM offers the following REAN-support and assistance for voluntary return: - Support before, during and after departure consists of return counselling and support to obtain a travel document.  

- An airline ticket and a small financial allowance to cover for the basic necessities after return.

- Depending on your nationality, you might be eligible for reintegration support.', 'Document: Can the Dutch Red Cross provide medical assistance?  

We can provide you with general information about healthcare and medical assistance in the Netherlands.

However, it is important to note that the Dutch Red Cross does not offer direct medical assistance.   

It might be confusing, as other national Red Cross societies may offer medical assistance in their countries, but the Dutch Red Cross does not provide this.', 'Document: I need a wheelchair or another permanent medical aid device If you need permanent aids, such as a wheelchair, for example because of a disability, you will usually receive these from your municipality.   

You can contact the Wmo-loket of the municipality you are residing in.   

You can also buy or rent a walker yourself, for example via the thuiszorgwinkel.

On Marktplaats you can also find cheap second-hand wheelchairs or walker.', 'Document: What can I do if I am not feeling safe at my host family?

Sorry to hear this.

There are a few options:     Are you in immediate danger?

Call 112.     

Contact a support organisation for assistance, information, mediatiation and more.

See for most recent information: www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety    You can always contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at home) at 0800-2000.     

You can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities if you no longer want to stay with your host family.

If you give your location, I can give you a registration point nearby.    

See for most recent information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/housing/regional-initiatives', 'Document: DTV (Repatriation and Departure service)

The DT&V helps foreign nationals return to their country of origin.

For third-nationals from non-EU countries who have fled from Ukraine they offer:  - Advice and information about repatriation and return.

- A one-way airline ticket.

- Assistance during departure from Schiphol Airport.

- In some cases financial support']

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', "Document: How can I get food support?  

When you are staying in a public shelter, please approach someone from the shelter to ask where you can find additional food support.

You can also contact the Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk.

For all general questions, new applications, extension requests, etc, PA's can call/text/

WhatsApp them at +31 97010259797 (Mon-Fri 9:00 – 17:00).  

In municipalities all over the country Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands) distributes food parcels to displaced persons from Ukraine.

Too find out if you are eligible, please see: https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/", "Document: I can't eat the same food as my host does

Yes, I understand that you used to eat different meals and some food can taste strange for you.

If so, you can always discuss it with your host.

I am sure, there is a way for both of you to find a balance.

For example, you can ask your host if it's not a problem for you to cook some meals for yourself.

If you already get social money, you can buy some products for your own use.

It's not an obligation to eat only the food your host eats every day.

You can use your money for food you prefer to eat.", 'Document: Red Cross The Red Cross focuses on humanitarian assistance, they offer for example; first aid, emergency food support and psychosocial support.  

Through the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp (https://wa.me/31614458781]) they can connect you to available help.', 'Document: Google Map with an overview of locations where humanitarian aid is being provided (e.g. food, clothing) https://goo.gl/maps/SvfGnjBnH8j9cYbA9', 'Document: Helpdesk Red Cross If you have questions regarding food, shelter, medical help, your situation or any other help you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp

[here](https://wa.me/31614458781)  General helpdesk from the Red Cross, we can help to connect you with the right help available.', 'Document: How can I get support with clothes?  

The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  

https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/  For most recent information on initiatives that provide support in clothes or offer clothes for a small price see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace', 'Document: I have HIV, where can I get support?

You can contact Service point of the Hiv Association and a volunteer from the association can answer your questions.   

https://www.hivvereniging.nl/blog/belangenbeschijning/13701-hoe-zit-het-met-hiv-zorg-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Phone: 020 - 689 25 77 (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 22:00)   

Email: servicepunt@hivvereniging.nl', 'Document: I have an eye condition, where can I get support?

The Eye Association advises and refers to the right authorities.

It can be about:  - Access to eye care: think of eye drops, injections or other treatments - Living with a visual impairment in the Netherlands: think of tools or building a network and learning the language  https://www.oogvereniging.nl/standpunten/steunpunt-migranten/steunpunt-oekraiense-vluchtelingen/

Telephone: 030-2945444  Email: ooglijn@oogvereniging.nl', 'Document: Website about financial support for Ukrainians during the war https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua/article/grosova-dopomoga-ukraincam-pid-cas-vijni-7738', 'Document: EnableMe UA EnableMe UA is a complete, up-to-date guide on all issues of disability and a friendly community for Ukrainians with special needs, mental disorders, chronic diseases and various disability groups.   

EnableMe Ukraine offers information, advice and online support to people with physical, mental or psychological disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua', 'Document: Is dental care reimbursed?  

This depends on your situation.  

Below is an overview of dental services that are covered by the insurance for Ukrainian displaced persons (RMO):   Conditions for providing dental care to Ukrainian displaced persons:  i.

The clinic can help patients living (registered) within a radius of 50 km from the clinic.  ii.

The patient must make an appointment through the special organization Tandartslijn (tel. 0881122112).  

iii.

If necessary, the clinic must provide proof of the record and argue the urgency (urgent necessity) of providing assistance.  

iv.

These conditions apply to adults and children.  

v. Compensation for adults

is limited to an amount of 250 euros per year and the choice of treatment - elimination of emergency pain with minimal costs.  

vi.

The amount of treatment is not limited to children under 18 years of age.

The only limitation is the exclusion of orthodontic treatment and prosthetics with implants and porcelain-ceramic crowns.   

The following types of dental services are covered by the RMO scheme:  i. Non-Periodic Review Consultation  ii.', 'Document: What is the stance of the Red Cross when somebody is not helped at HSP?  

We do our best to ensure that people arriving at an Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) are directed to the most appropriate form of assistance for them.

This could mean that people are directed to Ter Apel, rather than assistance being provided at the HSP.

However, we try to ensure that all refugees have their basic needs met, i.e. they can have some food and a drink, rest and charge mobile devices before travelling onwards.', 'Document: Access to medical care - Third party insurance - Living allowance (if asylum procedure has started) - Public transportation card - Education and development program - Payment of extraordinary expenses  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Locker - Night light - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Small towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Baby lotion - Washing up liquid - Washing machine detergent - Space for children - Space for men - Space for women  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV', 'Document: I want to return to Ukraine, where can I find support?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine who wish to return or continue their migration can receive assistance from the Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V).

Depending on the nationality and/or country of return or onward migration, they can provide return and/or reintegration support.                   

For more information in English and Ukranian, see: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine   You can use the contact form on the bottom of the following webpage of the DT&V to indicate whether you would like to be assisted in your return to Ukraine: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine   For an information video made by the Red Cross see: EN: https://youtu.be/PV-PJv-oCDw  UA: https://youtu.be/5YsAYFqYsjM  RUS: https://youtu.be/n_otbQncTHs', 'Document: Can I get financial support for a return to my country of origin?

If you have fled Ukraine, but do not have Ukrainian citizenship, you can no longer make use of the remigration support of the Repatriation & Departure Service (DT&V).

This financial support stopped March 4, 2024.   

Are you a third-country national from Ukraine and do you still want to return to your country of origin or another country outside the European Union?

IOM can assist you with REAN-return support and depending on your nationality you might be eligible for additional reintegration assistance offered by IOM and several non-gouvernemental organisations.  

The IOM offers the following REAN-support and assistance for voluntary return: - Support before, during and after departure consists of return counselling and support to obtain a travel document.  

- An airline ticket and a small financial allowance to cover for the basic necessities after return.

- Depending on your nationality, you might be eligible for reintegration support.', 'Document: Can the Dutch Red Cross provide medical assistance?  

We can provide you with general information about healthcare and medical assistance in the Netherlands.

However, it is important to note that the Dutch Red Cross does not offer direct medical assistance.   

It might be confusing, as other national Red Cross societies may offer medical assistance in their countries, but the Dutch Red Cross does not provide this.', 'Document: I need a wheelchair or another permanent medical aid device If you need permanent aids, such as a wheelchair, for example because of a disability, you will usually receive these from your municipality.   

You can contact the Wmo-loket of the municipality you are residing in.   

You can also buy or rent a walker yourself, for example via the thuiszorgwinkel.

On Marktplaats you can also find cheap second-hand wheelchairs or walker.', 'Document: What can I do if I am not feeling safe at my host family?

Sorry to hear this.

There are a few options:     Are you in immediate danger?

Call 112.     

Contact a support organisation for assistance, information, mediatiation and more.

See for most recent information: www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety    You can always contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at home) at 0800-2000.     

You can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities if you no longer want to stay with your host family.

If you give your location, I can give you a registration point nearby.    

See for most recent information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/housing/regional-initiatives', 'Document: DTV (Repatriation and Departure service)

The DT&V helps foreign nationals return to their country of origin.

For third-nationals from non-EU countries who have fled from Ukraine they offer:  - Advice and information about repatriation and return.

- A one-way airline ticket.

- Assistance during departure from Schiphol Airport.

- In some cases financial support']
